title: Payment Arrangements Desk Guide — Due-Date Changes, Restructures, Deferrals and Payment-Method Changes
content:
Consumers may ask to move a due date, restructure the installment, defer one installment or change the payment method on a plan under Payment Arrangements, and each granted change is recorded once on the plan's installment history and then written to the plan record.

## General rules for every kind of change

- Schedule and payment-method changes are granted only on a plan whose status is active, as the plan record shows.
- Each kind of change is limited per rolling 12 months against the type's allowance for that kind: due-date changes, restructures, deferrals and payment-method changes are each counted separately, as the changes of that kind recorded on the plan over the rolling 365 calendar days ending on the handling date, both ends included.
- The installments paid, where a rule below asks for them, are the distinct installments whose payments, not counting any payment that was returned, reach the installment amount less the type's partial-payment tolerance.

## Due-date change

A due-date change moves the next unpaid installment by no more than the type's largest shift in calendar days, in either direction, keeps a monthly due date on or before the type's latest monthly due day, and shifts every later installment by the same schedule; it never skips an installment.

Hypothetical case: on a type whose largest shift is 15 days, a next unpaid installment due on the 10th of a month may be moved to any day from 15 days earlier to 15 days later, provided a monthly due date stays on or before the latest due day; moving it 16 days is outside the rule.

## Restructure

A restructure is granted only after the installments paid reach the type's minimum installments paid before a restructure. The clause under which a restructure re-spreads the current arrangement balance over a new count of installments is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis. The new count of installments, counted with those already paid, stays within the type's maximums, and the new installment must satisfy the type's minimums and, where the type requires a budget review, the combined affordability test.

## Deferral

A deferral is granted only after the installments paid reach the type's minimum installments paid before a deferral. The clause under which a deferral moves the next unpaid installment to one period after the current final installment, extending the final due date by one period, is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis.

## Payment-method change

A payment-method change must be a method the type allows and takes effect on the consumer's new authorization, given the same way as at set-up.

## Revocation of automatic debits

A revocation of automatic debits stops a scheduled debit only when Ridgeline receives it at least the type's revocation notice in business days before that debit's due date; a later revocation stops the following debits, and the plan continues on manual payment only where the type allows manual payment, otherwise the consumer must authorize another automatic method before the next due date or the installment is handled as missed.

| Revocation received | The scheduled debit | Later debits |
|---|---|---|
| At least the notice in business days before the debit's due date | Stopped | Stopped |
| Later than that | Not stopped by this revocation | Stopped |

| Manual payment allowed by the type | After the revocation |
|---|---|
| Yes | The plan continues on manual payment |
| No | Another automatic method is authorized before the next due date, or the installment is handled as missed |

superseded_clauses: it moves the next unpaid installment to one period after the current final installment, extending final_due_date by one period
it re-spreads the current arrangement_balance over a new count of installments
